ApprovalKind.description:
What a human is being asked to approve (doc 03 task 3).

``plan``, ``escalation``, ``budget``, ``pr_open`` and ``merge`` are graph
interrupts; ``command`` is asked *inside* an agent turn by the runtime's
permission hook (2026-11-12 review, section 3.1).
ApprovalKind.title: ApprovalKind

ApprovalPage.description:
The approval inbox list, plus the workspace's pending count.

``total_pending`` ignores the list filters on purpose: the nav badge needs
one call that still shows the real count when the page is filtered.
ApprovalPage.title: ApprovalPage

ApprovalRead.description: An approval request and, once decided, its outcome.
ApprovalRead.title: ApprovalRead

ApprovalStatus.description: The outcome of an approval request; ``expired`` is the default-deny timeout.
ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus

ApprovalWaitSummary.description: Human wait time for approvals over a window (doc 18b).
ApprovalWaitSummary.title: ApprovalWaitSummary

CiStatus.description: The part of a GitHub checks rollup Gaia cares about (doc 15).
CiStatus.title: CiStatus

CostByDay.description: LLM spend for one UTC day over a window (doc 18b).
CostByDay.title: CostByDay

CostByModel.description: LLM spend for one provider/model pair over a window (doc 18b).
CostByModel.title: CostByModel

EventHistory.description: One page of a run's event history.
EventHistory.title: EventHistory

EventRecord.description:
The wire format of one event, and what the bus hands subscribers.

Persisted events always have an integer ``seq`` and an ``id``. A
``stream.gap`` marker is transport-only: it has ``seq=None`` and ``id=None``
and is never written to the database.
EventRecord.title: EventRecord

EventType.description:
Every event the bus can carry (doc 13).

``stream.gap`` is transport-only: the bus inserts it into a subscriber's
queue when that subscriber overflowed, but it is never written to the
``event`` table.
EventType.title: EventType

Principal.description: The authenticated caller, and the workspace every query is scoped to.
Principal.title: Principal

ProviderCost.description: Today's spend for one LLM provider.
ProviderCost.title: ProviderCost

PullRequestRead.description: A PR as the pull-request list route shows it (doc 15b).
PullRequestRead.title: PullRequestRead

PullRequestState.description: The part of a GitHub PR's state Gaia cares about (doc 15).
PullRequestState.title: PullRequestState

RepositoryCreate.description:
Register a repository.

``name`` is optional: the route defaults it to the repository root's
directory name. The commands are argv lists (never a shell string), and they
are the owner's registration-time values, never read from the repository.
RepositoryCreate.title: RepositoryCreate

RepositoryDetailRead.description: A repository with the two counts the dashboard shows.
RepositoryDetailRead.title: RepositoryDetailRead

RunStatus.description:
Where a run is in the graph of ARCHITECTURE section 4.

``awaiting_approval`` covers every human gate between agent turns, and
``paused_budget`` the budget interrupt. ``failed`` and ``completed`` are
terminal; a failed run is resumed from its checkpoint instead of being
revived by a status change.
RunStatus.title: RunStatus

RuntimeKind.description:
The harness behind an agent; ADR-001 (doc 08) picks which ones ship.

``native_claude`` and ``native_deepseek`` are the raw-API runtimes,
``claude_agent_sdk`` and ``cline_cli`` the harnesses. The values are stored
on ``agent.runtime`` and ``run.junior_runtime``, so they must not change
after the first migration without one.
RuntimeKind.title: RuntimeKind

StreamTicket.description: The short-lived credential the UI puts in the SSE query string.
StreamTicket.title: StreamTicket

TicketCreate.description: Open a ticket. ``status`` is deliberately absent (see the module docstring).
TicketCreate.title: TicketCreate

TicketPage.description: One page of tickets and the cursor for the next one.
TicketPage.title: TicketPage

TicketPatch.description: Update a ticket. ``status`` goes through the transition machine.

info.summary: Local-first control plane for a hierarchy of AI coding agents.
info.title: Gaia

get.description:
Answer without touching the database or the keychain.

A probe that failed because the database was busy, or the keychain was
locked, would report the wrong problem. "The process answers HTTP" is what
this says, and it is the only thing a supervisor needs.
Return the workspace's agents, newest first by UUIDv7 id.

schema.title: Response List Agents Api V1 Agents Get

get.description:
Return approvals oldest first, optionally filtered by status or run.

``total_pending`` always counts the workspace's pending approvals, whatever
filters the caller passed: the badge makes one call and must not change with
the page. ``ApprovalRepo`` keeps every read inside the authenticated
workspace.
Return the UTC day's spend, budget and per-provider breakdown.
Return the caller the bearer token resolved to.

Return runs, spend and approval wait metrics for the last UTC days.

The window covers ``days`` UTC calendar days ending today (UTC), which keeps
"last 1 day" aligned to midnight UTC rather than a rolling 24 hours.
Return the workspace's PRs, newest first, optionally filtered by state.
Return every repository registered in this workspace.

schema.title: Response List Repositories Api V1 Repositories Get

post.description: Validate ``local_path``, detect its origin and default branch, and add a row.

delete.description:
Delete the row only. No file or directory on disk is touched.

Refused with 409 while the repository has tickets or live worktrees: the
foreign keys cascade, so deleting the row would silently delete every
ticket, run, approval and usage record that hangs off it (lead review of 06).

get.description: Return the repository plus its worktree count and active run count.

Return events after ``after`` for one run, oldest first.

The run is loaded through ``ScopedRepo``, so a run in another workspace is
exactly the same 404 as a missing one.

Stream events with ``text/event-stream``.

A missing, used or expired ticket is the same 401 envelope; the route never
distinguishes them to a client. The ``Last-Event-ID`` header wins over the
``last_event_id`` query parameter (see the module docstring for why both
exist).

post.description: Exchange the bearer token for a short-lived SSE ticket.

get.description: Return one page of tickets, filtered by status, repository and title.

post.description: Create a ticket in ``repo_id`` after proving the repo is in this workspace.

get.description: Return one ticket, or 404 - the same answer for another workspace.

patch.description: Update text fields and apply a legal status transition, if one is given.

get.description: Return a repository's worktrees with orphan and dirty flags.

delete.description:
Remove a worktree from disk and mark its row ``removed``.

The row is kept as history. A dirty worktree is refused unless ``force`` is
set; a tampered worktree is always refused.
